text:
ana: Heads up — release pipeline blocked: typegen check failed for python-sdk after yesterday's OpenAPI tweak. Publishing v1.12.1 is blocked.

ci-bot: [CI] failure in job `typegen-check`
ERROR: Detected regenerated artifacts diff for `python-client`. Run: `make typegen && git status --porcelain`

tom: I see. The server added a new `Retry-After-MS` response header in the spec for better client backoff telemetry. It appears the generator emitted a new Header type and the committed files are out of date.

lee: minor, additive header. But our typegen output order changed across modules which trips the check. Two routes: regen and commit, or make the generator produce canonical ordering. Any preference?

ana: prefer to avoid noisy diffs in future. Can we make the generator sort components and headers before emission? That would keep commits stable across unrelated server changes.

tom: yes. The upstream typegen tool has a `--stable-output` flag (recently added). We haven't flipped it on in CI. I can patch the SDK build to pass that flag and re-run regen.

pkg-bot: note: changing committed generated files requires an entry in CHANGELOG and a semver assessment.

lee: semver? This is purely generated ordering; the public signatures are unchanged except new header type exists. I'd call it a patch: no API break.

ana: agreed. I'll open a tiny PR in the sdk repo to: 1) enable `--stable-output` in CI, 2) run `make typegen` and commit artifacts, 3) add changelog entry.

tom: pinging here when PR is up. Also will add a short unit test asserting that `components.headers` keys are emitted sorted so future regressions fail fast.

ci-bot: queued re-run for PR branch by tom.

pkg-bot: please add changelog line: `fix(devex): enable stable typegen output to avoid spurious diffs (patch)`

ana: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/428 (includes CI change + regenerated files + changelog). Local `make typegen-check` passes for me.

release-ops: I reviewed the changelog entry. This is a tooling/infra fix; patch release is OK. After CI green, merge and publish. Remember to land the canary tag so downstream packages can smoke-test.

lee: thanks team. Once merged, I'll re-run the release pipeline. Leaving this thread open until the canary finishes.

ana: merged after green CI. Tagging canary. :tada:

ci-bot: [CI] canary smoke run started for v1.12.1-canary.1

release-ops: all clear, promoting patch release.

tom: added a tiny note to the contributor guide about running `make typegen` after OpenAPI changes to avoid surprises.

ana: closing thread — learned: enable stable output in CI, add ordering test, and changelog requirement. Cheers.
